solution:
**Collar cells.**

The chapter gives this as character 4 of phylum Porifera: "These animals have special types of cells- collar cells."

The chapter's figure of the sponge Sycon labels the collar cells along the inner wall, together with the amoebocyte, the spicule, the ostium and the outlet or oscula. Cnidoblasts belong to a different phylum - the chapter gives them to Coelenterata / Cnidaria, where "Cnidoblast bearing tentacles are present around the mouth".

solution:
**Earthworm.**

The chapter states it as character 3 of phylum Annelida: "These animals are triploblastic, bilaterally symmetrical and eucoelomate." The earthworm is the first example the chapter gives for that phylum.

The three other animals named are placed elsewhere by the chapter. It uses the star fish as its own worked example of **radial** symmetry - "Radial symmetry ... Ex. Star fish. In case of this animal, there are five different planes passing through central axis of body". It calls Cnidaria, the phylum of the jelly fish, "radially symmetrical & diploblastic". And of sponges it says "Most of the animals have asymmetrical body", giving "some sponges" as its example of an asymmetrical body.

The chapter's own examples of bilateral symmetry are "Insects, fishes, frog, birds, human, etc.".

solution:
**Star fish.**

The chapter says so twice. Character 6 of phylum Echinodermata is "These animals have good ability of regeneration", and a "Do you know?" box beside the phylum's figure adds: "In certain situations, star fish can break apart its body parts and regenerate those later on."

Of the three other animals, the chapter records no power of regeneration. It does attribute good regeneration to sponges as well - "Besides, they have good ability of regeneration" in the Porifera list - but no sponge is offered here.

solution:
**Mammalia.**

The chapter prints Bat among the examples of class Mammalia: "Examples: Elephant, Human, Kangaroo, Dolphin, Bat, etc.", and its figure of the class is captioned "Class-Mammalia: Bat".

A bat is placed there rather than with the birds because the characters of Mammalia fit it: "Presence of mammary glands is typical character of mammalia", the animals are warm blooded, the body is divided into head, neck, trunk and tail, the digits bear nails, claws or hooves, and "Exoskeleton is in the form of hairs or fur". Class Aves is defined instead by an exoskeleton "in the form of feathers", forelimbs modified into wings and jaws modified into a beak - none of which a bat has. Flying is therefore not what decides the class.
